Volume 6, Entries for 1938 (translation)

Contains: January. 1. Last night this little man from Meran, Joffé, as I later found out, offered to go with me to Leptis. After some confusion, we set out at 10:45 with a driver from Tunis and arrived in Leptis at 12:45. We spent two hours among the imposing ruins. This Joffé has never heard of the Romans and asks whether these ruins are Spanish. He has a Kodak shop in Meran. Lunch at the Hotel degli Scavi in Homs. Back in two hours, and also arranged to go to Sabratha on Monday for two hundred lire. In town in the evening. Lachmann is beginning to grasp the local etiquette. 2. Another beautiful day. The German married couple want to join us on the trip to Sabratha. Walked into town. At the castle. In the afternoon, Suk and Jumo; walk to the cemetery with the Bersaglieri watchtower. At 19:11, a beautiful sunset and cannon shot; we walk down the river. Everyone stops and raises a hand, the automobiles halt, the cyclist jumps off his bicycle, and in front of me a boy falls off his donkey. What discipline! In town in the evening. 3. At 2 p.m., went with the Wagner Ettal couple in the Tunisian’s automobile to Sabratha. Deeply impressed by the ruins, which the Italians have extensively restored, especially the theatre. About fifty young Nazis at the hotel, one of them from Offenbach. In town in the evening. 4. Saw the hammam in town. Rain in the afternoon. Café. 5. Up at 5:00. With an unpleasant couple—a doctor from Milan—in the automobile to the Grand Hotel. Sat there in the “Pullmann” and drove into the desert. Sunrise. Coffee at the Hotel Djebel in Garian after the impressive climb up the winding road. Lunch at the Hotel Rumia in Jefren. We have a new “Neumann,” a venerable little fish [?] from Florence, who, being a bachelor too, has attached himself to us. Dinner and sleep in Nalut. Hotel Nalut. Mountains of ruined houses and the dry, torn-up landscape make it an apocalyptic picture of hell, while the hotel is perfect: everyone has a private bathroom with hot water. 6. Set out at 7:00. Sinauen. Tgutta. Picnic lunch in Derg. At about 16:00 in Gadames. Hotel Ain Fras. As Prinz Philipp said: the Thousand and One Nights, this underground city. The Arabs, very submissive, stand up and greet us as we pass. The Tuareg are prouder. In the evening I get onto the subject of Russia with the three Italians. There is also a Polish teacher, a young Jewish idiot from Cologne, Heidenheim, a Swedish couple, and our friends, the cameraman who speaks every language and the radio operator. 7. One party makes a camel cavalcade. We walk through the underground passages and the oasis. After lunch Lachmann and some others go on camels; we visit an Arab model house with the commandant, then take the “Pullmann” to a wretched little nearby oasis from which one can see the French border. At the Meharist barracks, where Frau Preto climbs onto a mehari [riding camel] to be photographed on it. With the commandant in the evening. 8. Set out at 7:00. Lunch in the automobile in Sinauen. Arrived in Nalut at 17:00. Climbed up into the Berber castle, a kind of wasp’s nest. Chatted with the so-called Count of War and earlier with a Swedish couple. 9. Set out at 6:00. First took a hot bath. Brief stop in Giado, where there is a labour service camp, as a reservist from Milan tells us there. Lunch in Jefren. Visited the caves and the underground synagogue of Tigrinna. Via Garan, at 17°C, to Tripoli. Thank goodness we have a room to ourselves in Mehari [? riding camel]. My eye is inflamed because I did not put on my dark glasses in time. Yesterday morning it was 2°C below zero in Gadames. Our “Pullmann” had a radio, but it did not work very well. A moment in town. 10. Seems to be a lost day. My shirt has disappeared, Lachmann’s money was in the waistcoat. But everything comes back. In town for the Arab slippers and at Tirrenia about the cabin. Went out again in the afternoon and walked through Uaddan. 11. In town morning and afternoon. Promenade by the sea in the evening. 12. In the morning, paid five francs in Paris and bought cheques. Coffee in the afternoon. Took the bus to the town of Trieste. Found the fisherman, Preto, Heidenheim. Nice cabin. Heavy seas. 13. Lovely sunshine. Arrived alone in Malta at 17:00. Errands for stamps and tea. English dinner at Barklay’s. Returned at 21:00. The singer from Naples tells of his life as a tailor and his hopes, and Lachmann shows a banknote, causing us a little panic. 14. Arrived in Syracuse at 6:00. Lunch at a café in town. At the post office Lachmann finds unpleasant news and begins to sulk without telling me why, spoiling everything for me. By bus to the Capuchin Latomia, then by carriage to Villa Landolini with the tomb of Plato, the Roman theatre, Latomia del Paradiso and the Ear of Dionysius, the Greek theatre. At the bank; Restaurant Archimedes, where Lachmann tells the ugly story of his fallen and treacherous friend. Departed again at 13:20 with the little fish. Delayed, at 17:00, Gardens. The peculiar bus ride beneath the porticoes. At Cook’s, who sends me to Flora. The room offered me there has no view. I find better lodgings at San Passerazio for 52 lire. Pension. Long walk with Lachmann. Dinner at the Savoy. Took the automobile to the gardens to fetch my luggage. Poor, busy Lachmann was left in Paradise and hobbled off to catch his train to Rome at 22:20. 15. Mosquitoes in the night. Wonderful weather. Lunch in the garden. Good food. Walk, coffee. 16. Greek theatre in the morning. Walk in Mazzaro and Taormina. Gardens. Return by bus. Tea in the dreadful tea room where there is dancing. 17. At Palazzo San Stefano-Spucches and the Gloeden house. He and his sister are dead. Baron Strempel lives there. Public garden. First letter from Gustav. Café. 18. No sun. Public gardens. Lantern tea room. Coffee. 19. Rain. Spent an hour sending my postal parcel to Meran. Haircut. 20. Checked out of Bel Soggiorno after Frau Prévé asked me to give up my room for new arrivals. Sad news of the death of Georg Massenbach’s only son. Konin. Tea at the Lantern tea room, expensive and not much to it. 21. To the station with the postman. Departed at 10:04. Express train. Changed at Messina; from San Giovanni an empty compartment, then a gentleman from Salerno. Arrived at 19:12. Carussi and Caso at the station. Lodged in Maria Förster’s room. Dinner with Carucci. 22. By carriage to the station, then Caso again. Departed at 9:20, in Naples at about 10:00. Walked to the market and Santa Maria del Carmine (Conradin), quickly ate soup at a dairy by the station. Express train departed at 13:00. In Rome at 15:33. Taxi to Pension Foggetti, Via Marchi 84. Took a parcel of letters to the Vatican, where everyone was buying stamps by the hundreds. At dinner we were very close together; unpleasant when one does not want to join in the conversation. A figure seems very familiar, and I learn it is director [Béla] Both, whom I saw at the Ungererbad. 23. At the Augustan Exhibition [“Mostra Augustea”], arranged in a way that interested me greatly. Music on the Pincio. Large crowd at the station. On the Corso in the evening. 24. Errands for Cordonnet. Philately on Via Ignazi, and left my suitcase next to the Renaissance exhibition, the textile exhibition. What interests me most are the old fabrics from the Middle Ages, papal pluvial [?]. I pull splinters out of my flesh, a very foolish experiment. Walk by Porta Salaria. 25. Vatican post office and St Peter’s. Zoological garden. Tea room at Piazza Pinciana. 26. By carriage to the station. Departed at 10:10. Alone in the compartment. Since it is raining in Florence, I continue to Bologna, 1544. Coffee at the Modernissimo. Cold and foggy. Dinner at the station. Departed at 19:53 in the Littorina. Cold and a bad smell of petroleum. Almost impossible to read because of the motion. 23:05 Bolzano. Changed trains at 0:06 for Meran. Kopp at the station. My old room at the Fortuna. 27. Errands and at the café. Gustav writes that Heidi really is going to marry his Frau Thomae. 28. Coffee at the Tappeiner and, in the evening, at the Dom-Raffel [?]. Margrit writes a desperate letter about Heidi’s wedding. The Gauthiers are in Arosa and talk of nothing else. Margrit wants Frau Merck to enquire about the Thomaes at the theatre. I reply that she has nothing to do with the theatre; Gustav should speak seriously with the Thomae couple. 29. Coffee and concert at the Kurhaus. Alone. Trenker film, “Condottieri.” 30. Snow. Café and concert at the Kurhaus. Finished B. Frank. 31. Departure from K. [Kobi?] for Obergurgl. Café San Valentino.
February. 1. Ran about for silk. Sankt Valentino. Reiner in the evening. 2. Walk to Café Bel Sito. On the 31st Juliana had a daughter. 3. Departed at 10:40. Three ladies in the compartment. Munich at 19:00. Room four. Dinner at Ove Höyberg’s. 4. At the Compagnia Italiana del Turismo (Cit), to tell them about our experiences in Syracuse involving the lire. Here I am received with a letter from headquarters. The commandant of the arboretum has written to the Italian ministry that the friend of Prinz Philipp from the Compagnia Italiana del Turismo (Cit.) in Munich had been misinformed. I explain my good intentions, and the head of the Compagnia Italiana del Turismo (Cit.) thanks me. I leave in triumph, but a little humiliated that my joker [?] ## [?] Philipp has pursued me all the way here! Lunch at Hahn’s. Tea and dinner at Ove Höyberg’s. 5. Major personnel changes among the generals and diplomats. What can it mean! Lunch with Frau von Lang at the Regina. Guest Ove Höyberg and Hans at Freising. Alone at the Kammerlichtspiele, “The King” in French. Very amusing. 6. Walked to Ove Höyberg’s for lunch. Tea at Biegeleben’s. Astoria cinema. “Der Berg ruft” with Trenker. Wagner-Bräu. 7. Visit to Otto Daum. Lunch at Klipstein’s with Renard, as always. Haircut. 8. Unexpected arrival of Lungershausen. The poor fellow must be operated on again. Lunch with him at Hotel Metropol. He left at 14:15. Tea at the Regina with Frau von Lang, Frau von Schieder and Morena. Dinner at Ove Höyberg’s. Hans in Switzerland. On returning, I find a telephone message saying I should not go to B. because the Lungershausens are coming here. 9. Poor Bodenheimer died yesterday, as I saw in the Frankfurter Zeitung. Ran into Ove Höyberg just as I was going to the post office to call him. Coffee at Kuhn’s. Dinner at Ove Höyberg’s. Saw “Schiffbruch der Seelen” with him. 10. Rain. Lunch at Ove Höyberg’s. The Lungershausens arrived at 15:11. With them at Professor Kielleitner’s, who prefers radiation to surgery. Dinner at Ove Höyberg’s. With him at the Prinzregententheater for “Richard III” (Golling, Just, Rösner, Balhaus, Hauptmann, Kersten). Dreadful snow. 11. Lunch with the Lungershausens. P. Hostrup, 3 Schellingstraße. Café Kuhn. Dinner at Ove Höyberg’s. With him at the Schauspielhaus for “Juchten und Lavendel” by Käutner. Stupid play. 12. Lunch with the Lungershausens, who leave for Berchtesgaden tomorrow. Café Kuhn. Dinner at Wagner’s. “Mutterlied” with Gigli. 13. Lunch with Ove Höyberg and tea. With him at Forstenhof. 14. Guest of Felix Ledebur at Preysing. Exhibition at Haus der Kunst. Dinner at Ove Höyberg’s. 15. Lunch and tea at Ove Höyberg’s. Expected Renard at the beer hall [Bierhalle?]. At my place. 16. Departed at 11:42. Tegernsee. By bus to Erneste. As I was getting off, I slipped on the road and injured [?] my right thumb. Returned at 19:00. Filmburg. “Camille” with Greta Garbo. Wagnerbräu. 17. Lunch at Ove Höyberg’s. Tea at Frau von Lang’s. Dinner at Ove Höyberg’s. Orlando di Lasso with him. 18. Lunch. Walk in the sun. Coffee at Kuhn’s. With Ove Höyberg. Fürstenhof. 19. In Karmeliterstraße. Looked at Don’s photographs, then at the other shop near Lenbachplatz. Here my sleeve is tugged: the Margravine of Baden; a strange encounter in front of photographs of her poor sister. I accompany her, and she tells me much that is new: the testamentary matter, still unsettled; Prinzessin Alice’s illness; Andreas, who wants nothing to do with her; the wedding in Athens; Theotokis’s appointment; Louis Ferdinand’s engagement to Kyra. We would have talked much longer had I not needed to go to the Klipsteins. Lunch with the couple, Mucke and Vollraths. Expected Renard at the beer hall [?]. Fanny. 20. Lunch at Rheinhof with Ove Höyberg. Listened to Hitler’s speech until 13:45, not realizing it would last three hours. Departure at 14:03. In Stuttgart a gentleman tells me the contents of the speech. In Darmstadt at 19:46. Dinner at the Schauroths’ and a telephone call from Prinz Lou asking whether I can come tomorrow. 21. Lunch at the palace with the Lous, Bück and Hardenberg. The Ludwigs [“Lous”] insist on giving me the tea sent to Potsdam. Ludwig holds me back to ask whether I would like an item of clothing or the Grand Duke’s raincoat. The difficulties with the will are not yet overcome. Herr Müller is not easy. The will dates from 1929, which explains the vexing gaps. Georg Battenberg is very ill after breaking his hip. Ludwig wants me to come again tomorrow. Condolences to Alfred Bodenheimer. 22. Lunch and tea at the palace. Prinz Andreas and Christo of Greece, drunkards, and the former’s foolish behaviour in Athens. Prinz Ludwig gave me two of his father’s suits and showed me the death mask. With Gustav and Heidi at Bender’s, also Michael. 23. D train at 11:42 to Frankfurt. At the Cronstetter Stift, saw Ablaing’s family trees. With Dietrich and Dietlind in Falkenstein. Returned from Frankfurt at 10:23 and 19:26. 24. Lunch with Schauroth and dinner. Schuschnigg’s speech, very impressive. 25. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Ehrhardt’s funeral. I had sent a wreath; Pastor Reit von Seebach gave a ridiculous sermon through his exaggerations, comparing Ehrhardt with Luther and who knows whom else. I preferred not to lay Prinz Lou’s wreath officially. 26. Lunch at Schauroth’s. With Gustav and Michael at Scheuerhof. 27. Visit to Leonhardi. Lunch at the palace with Lachmann. Walk with Lachmann and tea at my place. I gave him three pairs of boots and one pair of military shoes. 28. Took the tax return to the tax office. Lunch at Schauroth’s.
March. 1. March. Carnival. Lunch at Schauroth’s. 2. Lunch at Schauroth’s. At Scheuerhof in the evening with Bodelschwingh, Gustav, Hahn, Selzam, Westerweller and Harnier. 3. Lunch at Schauroth’s. At the police station about proof of life (Pension Office). Haircut. 4. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Cinema, “Verlobung auf Ehrenwort.” 5. Lunch at Schauroth’s. With Gustav at Scheuerhof. 6. Called on Merck, who was away, and Frau von Ramm, whom I met in the street. Lunch at the palace with Brother Geddes. Lachmann for tea. 7. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Walk in the sun with Gustav. 8. 9. Lunch at Schauroth’s. At the new Catholic church. Schuschnigg’s speech in the evening. He announces elections for Sunday. It seems very soon, and I tell Heidi he will easily be cheated if such superficial legitimations are enough. 10. Lunch at Schauroth’s. The newspapers do not mention the elections, but at 14:00 the radio announces that there will be an important message. After waiting an hour, a summary of yesterday’s speech is given, with the addition that the Berliner Tageblatt has published a sharp criticism of the elections, which cannot give an authentic picture of the situation when so poorly prepared and without even enough time to draw up lists. So the storm breaks, and many pessimistic possibilities come to mind. 11. Excitement about Austria. At Breitwieser’s about the Grand Duke’s clothes. Lunch with Frau von Leonhardi and the Max Heyl couple. Visit to the Wauers. 12. Schuschnigg resigned. German troops entered Austria. The National Socialist regime is established. Himmler and Heydrich in Vienna. Lunch at Schauroth’s. At Scheuerhof with Gustav and Bodelschwingh. Went out to hear Sprenger’s speech. 13. Hitler in Linz. Union with Germany proclaimed. Lunch at Schauroth’s. At 15:15 in Offenbach. Lachmann is enthusiastic about events. Returned at 22:00. 14. Parcel to Adolf with documents from Papa, letters from Max von Gagern to Grandfather, and things from poor dear Mother’s remaining belongings, in case Annemarie or Else wants any of them. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Yesterday the unhappy Maria asked me into her room to ask why I was so curt and unfriendly to her. It was my nerves’ fault if I really had been, but she should not complain again. I felt very sorry for her, but today I expected her to repeat the scene, since she had forgotten that she had made it yesterday. 15. Lunch with Frau von Ramm, General von Kleinschmitt and Hardenberg. Tea at Rotsmann’s with Frau Ehrhardt and General Ehrhardt, with whom I had a heated discussion. 16. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Prinz Lou sent for me. He wants my testimony that it accorded with his father’s intentions that he be the principal heir ahead of little Johanna, although Ludwig had not married a princess. I can confirm this to a great extent, according to what the Grand Duke told me last year at Wolfsgarten. I must accompany him. Ludwig and Hardenberg go tomorrow to the court, to probate judge Quack. Ludwig tells me that on the night after the accident he struggled with himself over whether it would be his parents’ will that, in these circumstances, he give up his Peggy; he thought he heard a voice telling him not to give up. 17. Up at 7:00. From the palace at 9:00 to the district court with Prinz Ludwig, Hereditary Prinz Hohenlohe and Hardenberg, where we meet notary Geisler and court chamber councillor Hermann. We are brought before district judge Quack, President Müller of the Higher Regional Court, and Best. The examinations begin; at 10:00 Prinz Philipp of Hesse and Regierungsrat Surkamp arrive. We wait for hours in the corridor, and I am the last to be called, only at 13:30. I am questioned, since I was the one to whom the Grand Duke confided his most intimate thoughts, about what the Grand Duke’s probable intentions would have been had he foreseen the present sad situation. I sketch the Grand Duke’s love for Donatus and Ludwig, how much he had come to terms with Ludwig’s marriage, and how certainly he would have approved of Ludwig’s conduct toward little Johanna, since he knew he could rely on Ludwig’s generosity toward her, and so on. Hohenlohe and Philipp also spoke with guardianship judge Schrimp. — Ludwig had heard from Philipp that he had been summoned to Hitler in Berlin last week, to be sent with a letter to Mussolini and told he must bring back an affirmative answer; Philipp was greatly relieved to receive Ciano’s immediate assurance that Mussolini would not oppose the Anschluss. Philipp assures us that Hitler’s action was entirely improvised and in no way planned. Philipp was afterwards in Vienna and seems to have played a very important role. Lunch with Gustav. Last night dinner at the Wauers’. 18. Lunch at the palace with Erbgraf Hohenlohe. Peggy’s birthday; she got a young “Schnauzer.” I had sent a cake made with a pastry press. With Gustav at the Helia for Sascha Guitry’s “Der Roman eines Betrügers.” Dinner at the palace with Neufville. Heard Hitler’s and Göring’s Reichstag speeches. 19. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Frankfurt at 15:14. Saw Lachmann at the Hippodrome. Show jumping. Saw his houses at Bockenheimer Landstraße 97 (bought for 82,000 [75,000 and 7,000]), Marburger Straße, and another one offered to him at Homburger Straße 15. Dinner at the Excelsior. Returned at 21:00. 20. The Schauroths in Wiesbaden. Lunch at the palace. First air bath. Letter to Alice. 21. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Second air bath. 22. Lunch at the palace, where I appear wearing an outfit belonging to the Grand Duke, which Prinz Ludwig notices as soon as he comes in. Haircut. 23. Lunch at Schauroth’s. I find Gustav in tears. Heidi has told him that her wedding to Frau Thomae will take place in a few weeks. Poor old man, having to endure this humiliation through this scandalous marriage. Third air bath. 24. Lunch at the palace with Prinzessin Christoph and Fräulein Paget. Fourth air bath. Dinner at the palace, also with Bück and Rittmeister von Bronsau. Paget is beginning to irritate me with her nicknames. 25. Encounter with Orth. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Fifth air bath. 26. At last, rain in the night. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Gustav starts up his tales again when I offer to accompany him in the evening, so I slip away and instead spend the evening on a sacred work in memory of those I have been mourning since last November. I began writing down everything I had not yet recorded about the last three weeks at Wolfsgarten, so that I could once more relive in thought the whole dear world around me. 27. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Lachmann for tea. 28. The postman from last year brought the money, much less than I expected, since the dividend was only fifteen per cent. I immediately sent 1,500 marks to poor Ove Höyberg. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Gustav came to his senses at Scheuerhof last evening. 29. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Read Münchhausen’s letters to Grandfather again. 30. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Telephone call with Bodelschwingh. Frankfurt at 18:06. At the Stift, then with Bodelschwingh at the Club for Trade, Art and Science. Address by Professor Rector von Arnim, whom I know from the war, after his raid on Reims. Very interesting. German-French relations. Two hours, witty. Dinner beside Herr Riese. Bodelschwingh had also invited the gentlemen von Rosenberg and von Wunsch. Returned at 0:35. I was woken again31. in Darmstadt, slept in. Lunch at Schauroth’s.
April. 1. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Read Roman’s and Fostner’s letters to Grandfather. 2. Lunch at the palace. They had been in Frankfurt with the Landgraves for Hitler’s speech. Philipp had not been seated in Hitler’s box. But when he sat down beside Sprenger, he did so anyway. Hitler called him over and asked where the Landgraves were, saying they should have been seated in his box. 3. Lunch at Schauroth’s with Marietta Rabenau. Lachmann for tea. 4. Lunch at Schauroth’s. 5. Lunch at the palace with the Hohenlohes, Schauroth and Marietta. Sent Münchhausen’s letters to Adolf. At the Großes Haus for “Tiefland” with Sattler. At Frau von Ramm’s and returned with Marietta. 6. Lunch at Schauroth’s. At Scheuerhof with Hahn, Westerweller, Harnier and Gustav. 7. Lunch at Ramm’s with Elisabeth Goertz, Gräfin. Called on Stephan, who is ill. Prinz Ludwig has left for London. 8. Lunch at Schauroth’s with Marietta, who leaves tomorrow. 9. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Visit to Fräulein von Rotsmann. Letter to the Dowager Marchioness of Milford Haven, Kensington Palace, London W.8, on the death of her son Georg Battenberg, apparently from bone cancer. 9. Heard Hitler’s speech at Schauroth’s. 10. Election day. Lunch at Schauroth’s. At 14:45 in Offenbach with Lachmann, Fräulein Förster and the Kanka couple. Returned at 22:00. 11. 12. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Haircut. 13. Lunch with Frau Else von Meister. At 19:13 in Frankfurt, Schauspielhaus, “Camille” (Käthe Dorsch), somewhat sobering. Maria Förster was there too. Returned at 23:20. 14. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Visit from Firnhaber. Since I last saw him, his father has died; he is in Seckmauern with his mother and sister. 15. Good Friday. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Wendland for tea. 16. Lachmann’s birthday. At 10:11 saw the Neumanns from Rostock at the station. Herrngarten with them. Coffee. Departed at 11:45. Lunch at Schauroth’s. 17. Lunch at Scheuerhof with the Gustavs. Lachmann on the motorcycle. 18. Gustav’s birthday. Schnapps and a tie. Heidi hunted for asparagus. Pleasant evening reading “Alexander I.” 19. Lunch at Schauroth’s. The Adelsblatt shows that Gustav’s grandmother, Berenhorst, descended from Wilhelm von Nassau and Coligny. After enjoying this enough, Gustav begins shouting today that he wants to hear no more of it because the Berenhorsts were illegitimate. A foolish argument follows, in which in the end one says more than one meant to, and the day is wasted for nothing. Letter to Carucci. 20. Hitler’s birthday. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Visit to Frau Stephan. Letter to Anna, Naples, about Vesuvius, and an air letter (55 pfennigs) to Renée in Batavia. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Bodelschwingh at my place. With him, Reitzenstein and Gustav at Scheuerhof. 21. Lunch at Schauroth’s. 22. Departed at 12:37. Changed trains at Stuttgart at 19:43. Munich. Room one. Dinner at Ove Höyberg’s. 23. Lunch and tea at Ove Höyberg’s. I had a pressed cake sent over. At the Luitpold cinema, “Jugend” by Halbe (Söderbaum, Braun, Klöpfer). 24. Music. Snow. Lunch and tea at Ove Höyberg’s. Café Luitpold. 25. Bought Ilseder Hütte shares on Edi Reitzenstein’s recommendation. Dreadful weather. Lunch at Hahn’s. Café Kuhn. Renard at the Brauhaus [beer hall?]. 26. Lunch at Klipstein’s with a pressed cake. Dinner at Ove Höyberg’s. 27. Lunch at Preysing’s. Café Kuhn. “The Pearls of the Crown” by Sascha Guitry, which I had already seen in Paris. Fürstenhof. 28. Lunch at Preysing’s. At Otto Daum’s home. Café Kuhn. Dinner at Ove Höyberg’s. With him at the Residenztheater for “Emilia Galotti” (Helmke, Renar, Fürbringer, Graumann, Lippert, Petersen). 29. Lunch and tea at Ove Höyberg’s. With Klipstein, since his wife has a cold, at the Gärtnerplatztheater for “Der goldene Pierrot” with Waldau, Walter Eich, Seibold, Karlstadt and Valentin. Pain in my leg. Wagnerbräu. 30. Lunch at Ove Höyberg’s. Coffee at the Daums’. Did not go out because of my leg.
May. 1. Lunch and tea at Ove Höyberg’s. Café Luitpold. The talkative old lady. 2. Lunch at Hahn’s. Called on Klipstein. Tea at Biegeleben’s. At the Brauhaus [beer hall?] with Renard. Poor old Fanny. 3. Sent ten marks to Else for her birthday. Lunch at Deutscher Kaiser. Departed for Berchtesgaden at 14:15. Christa at the station at 17:25. Radio in the evening. Hitler’s arrival in Rome. 4. Fritz had a very bad night. In the afternoon at Marietta Rabenau’s, who invites the Lungershausens on an outing to Lofer, but they decline. 5. At Fräulein von Rabenau’s in the morning. One act of “Aida” from Naples in the evening. 6. Letter to Alice. We meet Bassewitz. In town with him. In town with Christa. Concert at Piazza Siena. 7. At 11:00, with Marietta Rabenau by automobile to Rif [?] to the Ledebur couple. Lunch and coffee, sitting in the sun. At 18:00 continued to Salzburg, where Marietta showed me the cathedral. Festival Hall, Mirabell. Departed from Reichenhall at 19:41, to Munich at 22:07. Room five. Wagnerbräu. 8. Saw the 25-kilometre race at Dante Stadium. Renard. Lunch and tea at Ove Höyberg’s. Terrible news that they want to sell Höhenstraße 7. Poor Adolf. Café Luitpold. 9. D-Bank. Lunch at Klipstein’s. Letter from Adolf saying the general thinks the house is too small, thank goodness. Wagnerbräu. Olympia film, admirable. Wagnerbräu. 10. Lunch at Ove Höyberg’s. Went to the Ungererbad but did not stay. Haircut. Evening at the Brauhaus [beer hall?] with Renard. 11. Ungererbad. Lovely sunshine but a fresh wind. Ring Café. Rheinhof. Café Wien. Dreadful fashion show. 12. Ungererbad. Ring Café. Adolf wants to buy the house on Persiusstraße. Invited Ove Höyberg and H. to the Park Hotel. 13. Ungererbad. Klipstein’s maid forgot to say that I wanted to come for tea, so I go to the Ring Café. Preysing’s. Café Luitpold. 14. Ungererbad. Restaurant is open. Conversation with Herr von Tal. Dinner at Ove Höyberg’s. 15. Lunch at the Ungererbad. Herr von Tal again. Ring Café. Fürstenhof. 16. Lunch at the Ungererbad. The episode with the telephone, which still does not work. Dinner at Klipstein’s with the von Christen couple and Frau Stever-Boddien, divorced from Magnus’s cousin. She met the elderly Stevers in Milwaukee. 17. Visit from Ove Höyberg. Departed at 13:06. Changed trains at Stuttgart at 19:45. Heidi at the station. Dinner at Schauroth’s; Gustav is very weakened by influenza. 18. At Frau Gimbel’s. Frau Stephan in Viernheim will no longer take up her position with me; another chapter closed. Lunch at Schauroth’s. At Schauroth’s in the evening; he leaves for Aachen tomorrow. 19. Lunch with Maria. Brief air bath. 20. Lunch. At Hardenberg’s. In the palace in the afternoon. Prinz Ludwig invited me to Wolfsgarten for tea with Peggy and her sister-in-law. What sad memories, the first time after that tragic day on 16 November and in the Donatuses’ house. 21. Lit the stove again. Lunch with Maria. Visit from Bodelschwingh, who is going to Dragonerfest 7. Second part of the Olympia film. 22. Glenz could not find a housekeeper [?] for me. Troubling news from Bohemia. Visit from Bodelschwingh. Lunch with Maria. Got the wireless set working with batteries. 23. Lunch with Maria. Frankfurt at 14:48. At Oppenheimer’s, collected my securities. Tea with the Wendlands. Returned at 17:52. 24. Frau Bundschuh, Eschollbrücker Straße 44, introduces herself. Lunch with Maria. 25. Lunch with Maria. Letter to Kobi. 26. Ascension Day. Lunch with Maria. Air bath. 27. Lunch with Maria. Cinema: “Zauber der Bohème” with Kiepura and Marta Eggerth. 28. Lunch with Maria. Letter from Christa saying Fritz is very ill. At Bundschuh’s. 29. Lunch with Maria. Met Strastwitz [?]. Still reading “Gone with the Wind.” 30. Lunch with Maria. Lina’s birthday. Haircut. Cinema, “Yvette” (Dorsch). 31. Lunch with Maria. Air bath. Adolf and Gräfin Mellin, daughter of James Wolff.
June. 1. Wolfsgarten. At 12:00 in Wolfsgarten, where Lady Geddes, Peggy’s mother, is staying. In Kranichstein in the afternoon. Hardenberg for dinner. 2. Rain. Lieutenants Schwertfeger and von Gadow in the morning. In Darmstadt at the Porcelain Museum. Watched tennis. 3. In Darmstadt with Prinz Ludwig. In the afternoon, all of us went by way of Eberbach and Zwingenberg to Heidelberg. Dinner at the Schlosshotel. Returned by the motorway. 4. Happel is here; the others go with him to Darmstadt, where I return after lunch. In Falkenstein at 14:50. At dinner, Herr von Klöden Wennemar, Dietlind, Wörnle and Fräulein von Brandenstein. 5. Pentecost. Good Johanna’s hundredth birthday. From Kronberg to Frankfurt at 12:06. Lachmann at the station. Mosler bath. Dinner at the Excelsior. Rain. Back in Darmstadt at 21:00. 6. In Frankfurt at 12:52. Lunch with Lachmann at the station. Mosler. Excelsior. Back at 21:00. Meet Frau Römheld and father and son Mittelstaedt. 7. Air bath from 13:00 to 18:00. 8. Poor lunch at Reichshof. Air bath. 9. Lunch with Lina. Air bath. Dinner at Schauroth’s after their return; telephone call about the Lungershausens’ baptism. 10. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Air bath. 11. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Air bath with Gustav. Scheuerhof. Thunderstorm and rain. 12. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Lachmann for tea. 13. The day at Wolfsgarten with Hereditary Prinz Hohenlohe and his two children. Little Johanna seems to be coming down with whooping cough [?]. We talked for hours on end. Drove home at 23:00. Letter to Lisa Küchler. 14. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Air bath. Dinner at Wauer’s. Letter to Alice. 15. Sunday ticket to Nauheim at 11:41. Arrived at 12:56. Anna at the station. Parkhotel. Café Goeffel. Returned at 21:33. Letter from and to Alice. 16. Lunch at Schauroth’s. 17. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Haircut. 18. At Negenborn’s in the morning. Lunch at Schauroth’s. At 15:00, riding games at our barracks. At 18:00, meeting and dinner at the Casino. I sit between Fahr and Bernhardi. Afterwards at the barracks. 19. Travel agency about guilders. At the Traube, the two Lachmanns, Ahlefeld, Lersner, etc. To Kranichstein in the Krümper wagon. Lunch outdoors, between Bück and Frau von Flotow; Prinz Ludwig was there too. Returned with Issendorf, who told me about the complicated problems in Spain, where the social and political difficulties make a chaos quite unlike what one imagines here. Dinner at Fritz Merck’s with the Nettes [?], Lenski, von Nees, Lugershausen, etc. Walked home with Frau Andreae and Negenborn. 20. Lunch at Schauroth’s with the Lungershausens and Negenborn. Air bath. 21. Lunch. Air bath. Bodelschwingh. At my place and at Scheuerhof with Gustav. 22. At Wolfsgarten with Prinzessin Margarita. Two young English people: Margarita and Chesterton. Lieutenant von Berg and Kielmannsegg for tea. The Lenski couple for dinner; I walked home with them. I do not even think of Cecile’s birthday! 23. I am truly ashamed of myself. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Air bath. 24. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Air bath. 25. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Frankfurt at 14:43. Mosler with Lachmann. Returned at 20:15. 26. Lunch. As yesterday, at Mosler with Lachmann, and dinner at the Excelsior. Returned at 21:00. Packed. 27. At the travel agency about tickets and a letter of credit. Departed from Frankfurt at 11:31. To Potsdam at 12:15. Adolf at the station at 21:03. Taxi to Höhenstraße 7. 28. Frau von Tschirschky lives here. Annemarie and Inse for tea; I give them twenty-five marks. 29. 30. Brewer [?] Lehmann cancels. By automobile to Dietrich-Eckart-Straße 14. Inspected the house at Neubabelsberg. Café Bürgerhof. Dinner at the Tschirschkys’.
July. 1. Adolf in Berlin with von Löper; he is buying the house for 40,000 marks. I think he has done well, despite all the alterations that will be necessary. The Tschirschkys leave. 2. In town with Adolf and at Negenborn’s. A little rain. 3. For tea, Gräfin Mellin, daughter of James Wolff-Rodenpois, who lives with Prinz Eitel Friedrich of Prussia. Memories of Livonia and so many dead people. 4. 5. Dinner at Negenborn’s with Gräfin Bismarck and the nanny. She tells of Kyra’s wedding to Louis Ferdinand. They met at Johannisberg. Frau von Murzen was at the wedding and says she had to lend jewellery. Their Royal Highnesses first set 1 and 2 May. The Grand Duke of Mecklenburg forced them to give up 1 May and invite people for 30 April and 1 May. The Schachts [Schack?], Schwerin, Kronigk and Neurath went to the rout [informal reception]. The old Tsar of Bulgaria bought a beautiful sapphire necklace in Paris from the imperial Russian jewels and gave it to Kyra. Gräfin Bismarck spoke very well of Gräfin Mellin. Prinz Eitel Friedrich had seriously wanted to marry her. Auwi’s [August Wilhelm’s] son, the nice young man I saw at Wolfsgarten, wants to marry a divorced Frau Weigand, much older than he is; he was transferred to Görlitz, but the woman has already followed him there. The Prince’s mother favoured this sad mésalliance, but Auwi was very upset. The Grand Dukes Vladimir and Dmitri attended the wedding, as did Ileana with her husband, but the Brunswick family had declined. 6. Went with Adolf to Berlin to see the demolitions at Potsdamer Brücke, then the Brandenburg Gate. I returned alone from Friedrichstraße at 11:50. Adolf went to the notary; he still does not sign the purchase of the house, because he disagrees with some of the conditions they want to impose on him. 7. 8. Visits to the Stadtschloss. At Negenborn’s. Haircut. 9. By automobile to the station. Departed at 14:11. Changed trains at Hildesheim. At 16:28 in Nienburg, where Reitzenstein was waiting for me. By automobile to Eichhof near Liebenau. Dinner with the Krossa couple, the Lestocqs (she née Behr), and Frau Ruhstrat. 10. With Reitzenstein, Frau Ruhstrat and young Krossa by automobile through the forest, where rain caught us. By automobile to Verden. Riding tournament. After dinner at Krossa’s. 11. Walk with Reitzenstein. Lunch with the painter Plinza. Departed at 15:00 by automobile with Reitzenstein; after 17:00 at Kreftingstraße 3, Bremen, with the Wätjens. After tea, a walk to the cathedral, Old Town Hall, Waage, Essighaus and Böttcherstraße. Bought chocolate for Krossa and Tilde Wätjen. At midnight at the station with Reitzenstein and Wätjen. Departed at 0:02. Met Adolf in Hanover at 1:57; at 2:13 in the sleeping car. He tells me of Tschirschky’s agitation over the dissolution of the family fideicommiss. Via Bentheim. At the border we are told we must report to the police after the tenth day. 12. Dining car departed at 9:40 for Amsterdam. Haarlem at 10:12. Taxi to 24 Dreef, where Anna gave us a very friendly welcome. Walk with Anna in Sparre. 13. All of us took the tram to Amsterdam at 10:05. Colonial Museum. Lunch at Lido. Harbour tour and through the old canals. Returned at 17:00. 14. With Adolf at the Frans Hals Museum. All of us by automobile via Ymuiden to Zandvoort. Tea at the bathhouse. Returned by tram. Athletic parade. 15. By automobile at 8:00 via Alkmaar, to see the cheese market, through the Dam, Wieringen and Harlingen to Leeuwarden to the Hora Siccamas. After lunch, by automobile to visit a Frisian castle, once Heringa. Returned at 18:00, in two and a half hours. Letter from Balagué, whom I thought dead. 16. Letter to Balagué, Urgel 97. III. Through town with Adolf. 17. All of us at Bloemendaal and Heemstede for a walk. 18. By automobile to Noordwijk, Leiden, Hillegom. 19. Departed for The Hague at 15:00. Terminus Hotel. Same room as last year. In Scheveningen and dinner at the Krone, then café. 20. With Adolf to the archives and the Mauritshuis. Lunch at Pool. Along Denneweg to Javastraat. Stirum arrived yesterday. Adolf changes to number 93. Dinner at the Krone with Theo. 21. Errands on Noordeinde. In Scheveningen. Cloudy weather. Dinner at the Krone with Theo. Two girls quarrelling. 22. Our first bath in the sea; as far as Adolf is concerned, very little. He imagines he has been in the water. Lunch at the palace. Coffee. Encounter with Theo. Ate with him at the Krone. 23. Theo leaves. At the station with Adolf. Departed at 10:30. I feel sorry for him and all the difficulties facing him with his house. A pity about his affectations and his infallibility, with so many charming qualities. I am very grateful for his affection for me, but all the more sensitive when he shows a less favourable side. Errands. Bathed despite wind and clouds. Immediately afterwards the weather improves. Sat in the sun for hours. The boy questions what I paid. I give him a sharp dressing-down. Foolish Heinz and his fiancée. Bad dinner at the Kleine Deslen [?], Plein [square in The Hague]. 24. Bath and four hours in the sun. Pier. Good dinner at Pool. 25. Bathing in Haarlem. Tea and dinner at Anna’s at 15:15. Returned at 21:30. 26. Rain. At the aliens’ police office, 13 Alexanderplein. Waited a long time. Tea at the Gouden Hooft. Dinner at Pool. 27. Departed for Middelburg at 9:30. Lange Delft, Dam, Steenrots, Balans, Abbey, Lange Jan, town hall; lunch at the Dutch coffeehouse. At 16:00, with O.P. [?] by automobile to Veere and Oostkapelle, House Anthonia. In the dunes. Dinner with the lady, daughter, niece and nephew. All by automobile to Middelburg. Departed at 20:00. The Hague at 21:30. Haircut. 28. At Graswinkel’s, who wants to give Queen Wilhelmina’s letters from Wilhelm Alexander to the archive. Bathing. Strong waves. Milk at Landbau. Dinner at Old Dutch. 29. Bathing all day. Sierkan. Coffee at Pool. Letter to Alice. 30. Bathing. Heat. Sierkan. Conversation in German at the baths. Ilse’s birthday (fifty marks). Dinner at Old Dutch. 31. Bath all day. Sierkan. Café Pool.
August. 1. Errands. Bath. Departed at 14:28. Via Emmerich. Changed trains at Mainz. At 20:47 in Darmstadt. Taxi home. 2. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Air bath. Great heat. 3. 4. Lunch at Schauroth’s. With Gustav at Fink’s. 5. At Hardenberg’s. He is going to the Lous at Fischbach. Then they return here on the 15th and leave for Grainau and Tarasp on the 19th. This gives me the idea of asking whether I might come there for a few days at the beginning of September. Heidi’s wedding is on 3 September. Hardenberg says there is a war party in Berlin which Hitler has supposedly rebuked harshly, since he did not want these scoundrels to lure him into war. In addition, Hitler spread intrigues about a friend of Hardenberg’s, a museum director whom they wanted to get rid of. It is good to hear such facts. Hardenberg tells me about Heidi’s wedding. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Contrary to expectations it begins to rain, so I arrive at the air bath soaked. A beast [? bêtât], Herr Schreiber, introduces himself. 6. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Frankfurt at 14:43. The two Lachmanns at Mosler. Thunderstorm. Excellent lunch with Lachmann. Returned at 21:00. 7. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Lachmann calls to say that he is unwell and will not come to Frankfurt for the air bath. On my return I am called from the rear house. The young woman appears: she is looking for an apartment and wants two of my rooms. Frau Stein had said that my apartment was almost always unoccupied. A blow to me—so the first attempts to dispossess me of my apartment. Just as Negenborn predicted. We must resist by every means if the attacks continue. With Gustav at Fink’s. 8. Anna writes that Nino wants to come to Potsdam—and here he is! Lunch at Schauroth’s. Air bath in the rain. 9. At the travel agency they no longer accept contribution payments, as they tell me in very categorical terms. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Read Herzog Bernhard of Weimar’s letters. 10. Leonie Shelton arrives Saturday. Lunch with the Schauroths at Fink’s. Air bath. Yesterday I spoke with Frau Stein: “Don’t take it so tragically! I thought it would be a convenience for you to have this couple in your house, who would look after you, and I felt sorry for this young woman who can’t find anything.” 11. Bodelschwingh writes that I should come on the 18th and 19th, since Mechthild cannot stay. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Went back to the air bath but did not go in because rain threatened. Read Mother’s 1870 diary. Haircut. 12. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Heidi does not want my Venetian lamp as a wedding present. I give her a silver cigar box and my gramophone records. 13. Lunch at Fink’s with the Schauroths. At the station at 16:16. Leonie Shelton does not arrive, so my carefully prepared tea is for nothing. I return at 18:00 to the Piccolo at the Traube: the lady has arrived. I run to her. Neno is very kind and simple. Dinner at Scheuerhof with Gustav. 14. Miserable rain. With Neno to the palace, then Oberwaldhaus and Kranichstein. Lunch. Home for tea. Terrible thunderstorm and notice that a telegram has arrived. I was frightened. There was no way to telephone because of the storm. Later I learn it was from Anna, who had booked a room at the hotel for Neno. The Schauroths came by for a while. Dinner at the Traube with Neno. 15. Rain. Neno at my place at 11:00, looking through old Dutch photo albums. With her for a while at the Schauroths’ and the Traube. Lunch at the station. She departed for Amsterdam at 13:31. She kissed me goodbye so hard my gums cracked. She is so attached to everything connected with her father and has little affection for Jessie. 16. At Wolfsgarten with Prinz Lou and Peggy. They were invited to Berlin for the celebrations in honour of Horthy, but had to decline. Prinzessin Emma and daughter Elisabeth were in Doorn. Returned with them at 20:00. 17. Otto Daum announces the birth of a son, Gerhard Alfred, on the 15th. Lunch at Schauroth’s. 18. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Air bath. 19. Lunch. The Dutch consul Harts van Teklenburg came to collect a pile of Grandfather’s papers. Nearly had an accident with the tram. 20. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Lachmann cancels the air bath. 21. Lunch. Offenbach at 14:42. The young Harrison for tea. Returned at 22:00. 22. Lunch. Air bath. 23. Lunch. Good Adolf’s seventieth birthday. Processed stamps from Wendland. 24. Lunch. Air bath. Rode home by automobile with Rittmeister Müller. Frankfurt, Frankfurter Hof at 19:14. Dinner at Dietrich Bodelschwingh’s. Returned at 23:20. Telephone call with Lachmann. 25. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Packing. 26. Gustav at my place for a while. Took the tram to the station. In Stuttgart I missed the railcar train by one minute, so I only arrive in Munich at 19:46. Dinner at the station, telephone call with Wiedemann. Telegram to Heidi about her wedding tomorrow. Continued at 20:55. Changed trains at Rosenheim, Kufstein and Wörgl, where I waited 45 minutes for the delayed express from Vienna. Arrived at 12:45. Hotel Union, Innsbruck, where Lachmann had booked a room for me when he arrived yesterday. 27. Walk with Lachmann. Sat in the park. By bus to Ambras. Walked through the park to the baths. Lunch there and sat in the sun. Wonderful view. Walked back to town through the forest. Café Maria Theresia. Walk along the arcades to the bridge, where we parted. Talked with me for a long time. Returned in heavy rain. Dinner at the hotel. 28. Schönruh open-air swimming pool. Departed at 17:15. Great delay. Landeck, Hotel Post. Dinner at the hotel. 29. Telephone call with Dietlind about the wedding. Short walk. Bus at 14:10. Arrived at 16:30 with a Greek at Schuls Post. Telephoned the castle to report our arrival. Coffee. Prinz Lou arrived with Frau Stokowski, who immediately continued on, and Hardenberg was at the castle. Prinzessin Peggy was there when we met. I occupy two beautiful rooms and a bath on the second floor. 30. Visit from the Pinösch couple. With Lachmann at the tea house. After lunch, long conversation with the four of us. After tea, down to Dr Federspiel’s and to the monastery. Telephone call with Lorius. 31. The Ludwigs [“Lous”] and I drove by automobile to St Moritz at 10:30. The Ludwigs invited us to a mediocre lunch at the Hotel Albana and coffee at Hanselmann. Onward via Silvaplana to Sils Maria. Walk in the rain at Chastè. Nietzsche memorial plaque. Long conversation after dinner.
September. 1. At Federspiel’s. Lunch with artichokes and champagne for Graf Bernstorff, who came from Vulpera. Lou drove us to Schuls. We departed at 16:20. Landeck. Hotel Post. Yesterday stopped in Zuoz to see the Hotel Concordia where the Stirums will stay. We are both delighted with our stay in Tarasp, with the kindness and attentiveness of the Ludwigs [“Lous”], and with this magnificent castle. Visit in the morning from Fanzun’s son-in-law. 2. Hardenberg arrived at 11:30. Departed with him at 12:03. Lachmann and I got off at Ötztal. By automobile in three hours to Ober-Gurgl. Lunch in Umhausen. Changed at Zwieselstein. Welcomed by Pastor Schöpf. Pension Jenewein. The son, a friend of Kopp’s, did not arrive until evening. Primitive rooms. For dinner, two elderly Bardeleben ladies, very talkative. Three hours in Ober-Gurgl. 3. Walk and sit in the sun. Coffee at the hotel. Gurgl. Rain. 4. Telephone call to Innsbruck. Departed at 11:20. Bus very full. At 14:15, Ötztal Café. Departed at 15:18, delayed. In Innsbruck after 18:00. Hotel Union. Pessimistic letter from Adolf. Dinner at the hotel. Arcades. Café alone. Taxi. 5. Upset stomach. Disaster in bed. Hofgarten. Looked at guesthouses. Lunch at Union. By bus to Igls. Haircut. Café Bozener Platz. Dinner at Großer Bär. 6. Lunch at Großer Bär. Bozener Platz. Looked for money at the post office. Großer Bär. Agitated letter because we had run away. 7. Departed at 18:20. At 16:15 in Zell am See. Hotel Excelsior, fourth floor, with a splendid view. Room costs nine marks. We like it very much. Crossing the lake. Coffee at Sonneck. Walk along the quay after dinner. 8. Zell am See. Lovely sunshine. At the beach bar in the morning. At 14:00, Schmittenhöhe. Coffee at the summit. The sky clouds over. 9. Fine weather. In Bad Gastein at 13:53. Arrived late at 15:45. Bodelschwingh House. Landhaus Savoy. Coffee at his home. Everyone at the station. Arrival of Frau von Golzani. We left at 17:42. At 19:30 in Zell. 10. Letter from Marlene saying her father is very ill. Conversation at 14:30 with a man from Salzburg who works in Mittersill. Changed trains at Schwarzach. Lachmann [?] directed [?] on to Salzburg at 17:00. Confusion over Hotel Hirsch; there are two in Salzburg and our telegram went to the wrong one. At last, by taxi to the Goldener Hirsch on Getreidegasse, a strange old building. At the post office and Café Glockenspiel. Rain. Dinner at the Hirsch. 11. Heavy rain. Berchtesgaden at 11:10. Finke at the station. Taxi to Falkenfels. Karlhans and Margot. Fritz has slept peacefully since last evening, but with such healthy breathing that it seems as though this might go on. At 16:30 I go up once more to say a final farewell. With Karlhans at Schwöbbrücke. Departed Berchtesgaden at 17:10. Dinner at the Hirsch. At 21:00 Finke telephones that Fritz died at 20:05 without waking. At least it was a gentle death. A strange coincidence that I should have been in this area on the day his hour struck. 12. Telephone call with Marlene. Cremation tomorrow. Telephone call with Gustav. With Lachmann to Hohensalzburg. Lunch upstairs. At Mönchsberg. Down by the lift. Café Bazar with Lachmann, who goes to Traunstein. Still at the Bazar with the Finkes and Karlhans. Telephone call with Prinz Lou at Unter-Grainau. Führer’s speech. No doubt any longer that there will be war if there is no yielding and the Sudeten Germans are not given self-determination. Dinner at the Hirsch. 13. Run to the flowers. By bus to the cemetery. Marietta Rabenau, Gräfin Waldersee, the Pönsgens, Bolongaro, Fräulein Kirchhof, the Bergens, Frau von Megern, etc. At 14:30, the very solemn cremation of old Fritz Lungershausen. By automobile with the Finkes. All of us for tea at the Österreichischer Hof. Driven to the station. Departed at 17:50 on an earlier train. Graf Meran from the Eisenerzberg, on his way to Vereinigte Stahlwerke. He knows the Ledeburs. I pick up Sepp in Munich, and we wait for Lachmann. Arrival from Traunstein. At Deutscher Kaiser. Lachmann unexpectedly meets L. [Lachmann?]. Room number five. Very worrying political situation. 14. With Lachmann at the Ungererbad. Beautiful day. Telephone call with Frau von Klipstein. Café Sendlinger Tor Anlagen alone. Dinner at Rheinhof. Walked home alone. 15. Chamberlain with Hitler, accompanied by the hopes of decent people. Lunch at Preysing’s. Café Sendlinger Tor Anlage. Dinner at Bratwurst Glöckle. Cinema: “Ehrenlegion,” “Die Frau des Anderen.” Spöckmeier. Telephone call with Frau Hirth. 16. Fine weather. With Lachmann at the art exhibition. Lunch at Reitbahn Restaurant. Staatsgalerie, Altdorfer exhibition. Coffee. Dinner at Rheinhof. Cinema, “Heimat,” by Sudermann, with Zarah Leander and George. Wagnerbräu. 17. Ungererbad. At 14:00, with Lachmann to Garmisch. The Hirths at the station. With them to Unter-Grainau. Admire the house. Tea with Frau von Wätjen, Herr Voidt from Heidenheim and others. Visited the old Preetorius couple. At the station with the Hirths. Returned at 16:55. Dinner at Excelsior. Lachmann backs out again. 18. Lachmann departed at 8:18. Left at 9:00, delayed, for Wiessee. At Ove Höyberg’s. Quellenhof. Lunch with Anna Rex. Tea with her at Erneste’s, Frau von Lang and a young lady. Dinner at Ove Höyberg’s. Returned at 20:18. 19. Anna has given me a cold, the first since 19 September 1937! Ungererbad. Café Sendlinger Tor. Dinner at Klipstein’s; only Dieter Klipstein was there. 20. Sitting in the Hofgarten and at Sendlinger Tor. Coffee at 10:00 in bed. Fort. 21. Bad night. Ungererbad. Sendlinger Tor. Coffee. Fox with him at 19:00. Brauhaus [beer hall?]. Despite everything, Fanny happened. 22. Ungererbad. Tea at Klipstein’s. Ate too much at the Excelsior and could not sleep, waiting to see what would happen in Europe after the conference. 23. Gustav writes that Hardenberg is in hospital after a car accident! It never ends for us! Waited at Odeonsplatz at one o’clock, since the trams were not running because troops were marching. Ungererbad. The same wait on the way back. Café Sendlinger Tor Anlage. I write to Hardenberg asking whether he wants me to come home. Dinner at Excelsior Fürstenhof, where I have the most joyful, well-fed reunion. 24. Errands. Ungererbad, where I write to Lachmann. Rain. Café Sendlinger Tor. Excelsior. Café Luitpold. 25. Departed from Wiessee. Lunch at Ove Höyberg’s and coffee with Anna in Abwinkel. Political discussions. Ove Höyberg is actually a woman in his deliberations. Nothing more can be expected of Anna. Already back from Gmund at 19:40. Bratwurstglöckle. 26. Glorious weather. Ungererbad. Sendlinger Tor. Haircut. Had my hair cut. Heard Hitler’s speech at the Pschorr with Martl. The broadcast was very indistinct and his voice very hoarse. One can hope that they will intimidate one another with threats until Beneš feels compelled to yield, and that in this way a disastrous war will be avoided. Martl drives me home in his automobile! A real transformation of things. 27. Even nicer boy at the Ungererbad. Letter to Negenborn about his seventieth birthday. Café Kuhn. Dinner at Ove Höyberg’s. 28. Ungererbad. Sendlinger Tor. Coffee. Here is moving and hopeful news: Mussolini, Chamberlain and Daladier are coming to Munich. Full of renewed courage at the Brauhaus [beer hall?], where Renard arrives in splendid condition for Fanny. 29. Huge crowd when the statesmen arrive. No trams in the centre. I take a long detour to the Ungererbad. Sendlinger Tor. C. Dinner at Ove Höyberg’s. 30. Louise arrives in the morning with the happy news about the agreement signed during the night. What a blessing. May the world learn from this lesson: reasonable, well-intentioned people can always get along if they sit down at the same table. There are always disagreements, but there is no need to bash each other’s heads in over every little thing. Besides, one can now say it was a diplomatic masterpiece, the way our Hitler got out of the affair and acquired a fine piece of Bohemia for Germany. — It is Lachmann who returns here tomorrow evening. Heavy rain. Met the Klipsteins. At Haus der Kunst at 15:00. While we look at the exhibition, Hitler comes and goes into the café. I invite Klipstein so we can see Hitler’s table and Ribbentrop too. Dinner at Excelsior. Café Luitpold, where Hungarian boys play little monkeys.
October. 1. Miserable rain. Invitation from Felix Ledebur. Lunch at Preysing’s. Café Kuhn. Dinner at Klipstein’s with the Caracciolas. 2. At the station with chocolate for Anna’s departure at 9:18. I reproached her for the political foolishness she indulges in. Lachmann arrived last night. Lunch with him at Neue Börse. Tea at Klipstein’s, where I left my galoshes yesterday. Dinner at Excelsior with Lachmann. 3. Rain. Errands. Café Kuhn. Dinner at Ove Höyberg’s. 4. Lunch at Hahn’s. Station cinema. “Verwehte [?] Spuren.” Looked at Rösler, then roast chicken with Lachmann and the Keyserlings on the Wiese, without speaking to them. With Lachmann at Ring Café. 5. Renard telephones. Alone in the Hofgarten in the sun. With Lachmann at Café Gassner and the Kurbel cinema: “Amphitryon.” Dinner at Excelsior. Führer speech: Winter Relief. Telephone call with Preetorius. 6. Telephone call with Stockhausen about Heinz Bodelschwingh’s wedding. Lunch at Ove Höyberg’s. Hans had to go to Berlin. Tea with Lachmann at Klipstein’s. Schauspielhaus: Shaw’s “Caesar and Cleopatra” (Domin: Caesar). Met Mongelas. Torgelstube. 7. Coffee at the Tierpark. Dinner at Excelsior. Letter to Neno. 8. Lunch at Neue Börse. Expresso [?] coffee. Lachmann departs at 17:00 for Ansbach. With Renard. Brauhaus [beer hall?]. Excellent Fanny. 9. One year since the Grand Duke’s death. Tierpark. Dinner at Deutscher Kaiser. Café Luitpold. Scarpi. 10. Hellabrunn. Lunch. Coffee at the Daums’, the baby. Cinema. Trenker film “Liebesbriefe aus dem Engadin.” Roter Hahn. 11. Rain. Lunch at Hahn’s. Cinema, “Helden in Spanien.” Dinner at Rumpelmaier. Fürstenhof. Cossack band. 12. Bought provisions at Hahn’s. Departed at 12:00 by railcar. Stuttgart at 14:30. Walk in the Schlossgarten and café. Departed at 16:47 for Darmstadt; the apartment was locked. Taxi to Frau Bundschuh, who had locked up again after Bodenheimer opened the door! Else has already left Wiesbaden. 13. Safe, etc. Lunch at Hotter’s. 14. At Hardenberg’s. At 17:00 with Prinz Ludwig to Wolfsgarten. Returned after dinner. 15. Lunch at Fink’s. Reading in the gardens. 16. Lunch at the station. In the gardens, where I fall asleep—old man. Lachmann, who had a motorcycle accident yesterday, for tea. Read Russian diary, 1908. 17. Lunch at the station. Stamp additions. 18. Lunch at Fink’s. Haircut. 19. At Hardenberg’s. Prinz Lou is there too and takes us to Wolfsgarten for lunch. Hardenberg lives in my room from last year, and all those memories overwhelm me when I enter it. Ludwig says that Alice of Greece was here four weeks ago, and that her premonitions and prophecies are astounding; for example, everyone in the family of Hesse named Georg rather than Ludwig dies young. Ludwig leaves for London tonight. Letter to Neno at K.L.M., Amsterdam. 20. At Maria’s, returned from Monsheim. Lunch at Fink’s. Visit to Wauer’s. 21. Lunch with Maria. Riding tournament. We have invited the schools. I have difficulty finding a place among the girls. 22. Lunch with Maria. At the tournament with her. It is pointless to have seats costing three marks, since we soon leave the grandstand, where nobody is, to sit in the sun. Around 22:00 a great commotion: Marlene wants to break into my apartment with her husband. I speak to them only from the window. A strange idea, to surprise someone. 23. Lunch with Maria and the Finkes. Lachmann for tea. 24. Good Mother’s hundredth birthday. At the cemetery with a wreath and many thoughts of the past. Lunch with Maria. She and the Finkes for tea at my place. 25. At the cemetery again. Lunch with Maria. 26. At the cemetery again. Lunch with Maria. Visit to Frau Merck. 27. Lunch with Maria. Brief visit from Lachmann. 28. Woke late; my head is muddled. It is as though I had a slight stroke in the night; my memory is failing me. Lunch with Maria. Met the Westerwellers and took a short walk with them. I am convinced that something in my head has changed since yesterday. 29. Letter to Alice. Lunch with Maria. 30. Lunch at Fink’s. Lachmann for tea. Dragon memorial association. 31. Lunch with Maria. Cemetery and at Hörr’s, Weinbergstraße 4.
November. 1. Lunch with Maria. 2. Lunch with Maria. In the evening Bodelschwingh came and collected the group [porcelain group?] “Chaste Love,” which I had given him at his request, and the Venetian lamp, a wedding present for Dietlind Pfaff. He told me about Stockhausen and Frau von Golzani. Dinner with him at Scheuerhof. 3. Lunch with Maria. 4. With Hardenberg. At 10:45 by automobile to Echzell to visit Wolfram Harnier; another daughter and son, Adolf, an aviator, a handsome boy. Harnier showed his lovely paintings: a portrait of Prettlack by Rigaud, the Duke of Lorraine, Tilly, supposedly Alba by Velázquez, and an album of miniatures by his grandfather, portraits and sketches of the old Grand Herzog Ludwig I of Hesse. Returned after tea. Heavy rain. 5. Maria in Kronberg. Lunch with Lina. 6. In Offenbach at 14:04. Fräulein Förster says Carucci has a son after three months of marriage! What an idiot. Returned at 22:01. 7. Lunch with Maria. Letter to K [Kobi?]. Too cloudy to see the lunar eclipse. 8. Lunch with Maria and her lodger, a Russian, director of a Russian church choir. Haircut. 9. Lunch. At the Kleines Haus for Möller’s “Untergang Karthagos.” Play with very crude effects. Pälzig remarkably good. 10. At a shop on Elisabethenstraße they showed me the aftermath of a pogrom organized that morning because a Jew in Paris had murdered Legationsrat von Rath. The synagogues here too were set on fire. I wonder only what will become of Bodenheimer and the other two Jewish families living in this house. Who could have foreseen this dreadful dilemma when I moved into my house in 1905! Lunch with Maria and the Russian. Tea at Wauer’s. On the way back I learn they have “looked for” Bodenheimer. Kemal Pasha dead. 11. Lunch with Maria. In the sunshine in the gardens. 12. Lunch. Gustav returns from Zuoz at 20:00. Heidi also comes to dinner with her “Ly,” whom I saw for the first time. A real shock, how ugly she is: an impossible nose, a dreadful mouth, yellow hair; the famous thin legs look like rickets or a child’s. She may have a good heart, but she is more like a servant. I understand why her husband is happy to hand her over to Heidi, but it is a disgrace for Heidi to have sacrificed everything for such a person, just because of her absurd legs. My position between honesty and my friendship with the Schauroths was very difficult. I played the joker to save the situation and because Heidi, with his sharp wit, which catches every quip, led me into it. Then we reproach one another, because it is always a little at the expense of poor, foolish Maria and also Gustav, who grows more foolish in his old age. I dread the moment when he asks me, “What do you think of her?” As long as he does not pester me with his dithyrambs about “the most beautiful legs in Darmstadt,” I hope I can behave myself. 13. Lunch at Schauroth’s with the Heidis. Lachmann for tea. 14. At the palace I meet Hardenberg. He is busy giving a radio lecture about the palace museum in the Madonna Room. I accompany him through town to Wauer’s house, where he is invited to lunch. I do not know that I am speaking my last words to him at the corner of Riedeselstraße. I go to lunch at Fink’s, since the Schauroths are invited to the Pertschs’. 15. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Melancholy memories lead me to reread Grandfather’s letters to his mother from 1838, Mother’s year of birth. The bell rings at 23:00. Lauterbach, reeking of alcohol: “Seeing that you had a light on, I came to tell you that Graf Hardenberg died an hour ago. He had heart trouble last evening and was taken to Alice Hospital this morning.” Prinz Ludwig will come to the palace later. I dress quickly, and Laun picks me up by automobile. At the palace are Prinz Lou, Chamber Director Herrmann, Frau Lauterbach and Fräulein Hermann. They discuss what is to be done and postponing the church service from the 16th to the 20th. Prinz Ludwig was with Hardenberg at 18:30 and found him very talkative. I learn from Sister Lena von Wedekind that the pains returned in the evening and that he died suddenly at 20:30 [probably 21:30]. The previous night he had called Happel to come because he was in great pain. Happel found him with a completely blue face, serious symptoms of angina pectoris and almost no pulse. Happel stayed at the palace for the rest of the night. 16. We all went from the palace to the hospital at 1:00 in the night. The poor deceased looked very peaceful and beautiful. At the palace at 10:30 in the morning. I advise Lou to telephone the news to Wambold, suggesting that he pass it on to Sprenger if he thinks fit, since Sprenger wanted nothing to do with Hardenberg. With Ludwig at Wolfsgarten. Lunch with Prinzessin Heinrich, Johanna Laubach, Gräfin, Frau Trench and Georgina. With Ludwig, drafted the announcement he will place in the name of the House of Hesse. Everyone at Rosenhöhe, laying flowers. There were enough people there. With Ludwig to the station to meet Fürstin Dohna. I go home. On the 15th of last year, probably exactly at 21:30, Prinz Don said to me: “Care must be taken that Hardenberg chooses a successor in good time, even if one of his nephews, for I distrust his heart. He could drop dead any day.” Now that was an accurate prophecy! They say Lou wants to take over Hardenberg’s work. In the long run, though, he will no longer feel free and will look for a successor to Hardenberg. In my opinion he should turn to Wätjen. — Gustav came to my house and asked for details. Then the bell rang again: a certain Adam Kolb II from Sickendorf, who says he has tried to find me many times at home. He served in the artillery, and I know him in one way or another from the war. I wonder what he could want from me now. 17. Bodelschwingh writes that Dietlind’s husband Pfaff died of a stroke yesterday morning! At the palace: Archivdirektor Herrmann, Fräulein Herrmann’s father, who worked in Hardenberg’s office, died this morning! Lunch at Wolfsgarten with Prinz Lou; as yesterday, the Margraves of Baden and Fürstin Dohna are also there. Returned with Prinz Lou. Yesterday he was in Hardenberg’s room with the brothers Rudi and Hanni Hardenberg and the nephew. There was a will. He leaves everything to his family apart from a few bequests. They say there is not much money. A pile of letters marked “destroy after my death” was immediately burned in the stove. Lou was surprised not to find a single letter for himself. — Ludwig wrote a very fine epilogue for the radio. From Wolfsgarten I telephoned Frau von Gebsant [?], Falkenh. 18. A moment at the palace with Prinz Lou and Erbgraf Hohenlohe. Lunch with Gustav. Hardenberg had often spoken with Margrit Stirum, saying he had a married daughter. We shall see whether she comes to the cremation tomorrow. At 18:00 at Gustav’s for a radio report on Hardenberg, a conversation about the palace. What a feeling, hearing that voice, full of good humour and sarcasm. 19. Up at 7:00. In Frankfurt at 9:30; tram to the cemetery for the funeral of poor Vicar Pfaff. Eva, Heinz’s wife, is not at all pretty. Poor Dietlind was quite moved. Returned at 12:07. Lunch at Schauroth’s. With them at the Schlosskirche at 14:30. Memorial service for Hardenberg. Large crowd. His compositions were played and sung; I found the effect mediocre. With Fritz Merck and Wätjen at the crematorium, where it was nearly over when we arrived. Lachmann for tea. At 19:00 dinner at Fritz Merck’s with Frau von Oertzen, her sister, Gräfin Büdingen and Wätjen. Merck was away; his wife disappeared during dinner because of a migraine. Wätjen went from the cemetery to the Traube to visit the Hardenbergs. At tea he sat beside a lady who told him she was Kuno’s daughter! Returned by automobile with Frau von Oertzen. 20. Long visit from Gustav. At 12:30 with Wätjen to Wolfsgarten. Very hoarse. For Ludwig’s birthday I brought a little book by Uexküll and Lachmann’s poems by Usinger. On the way back Wätjen told me that, as Gröning had told him, there had been a misunderstanding between him and Lachmann, and he would be glad if it could be cleared up. At 20:00, memorial service at the Stadtkirche. 21. Still very hoarse and coughing. Lunch with Gustav. Should one really risk moving into Hardenberg’s apartment on Zimmerstraße? Everyone praises it, and Prinz Lou strongly advises me too. With him, in pouring rain, to Herrmann’s funeral. Someone faints. Is this perhaps another sudden death? Ludwig tells me Kuno left two daughters, one of them a dancer. As she was travelling, they could not notify her. I also visited Zimmerstraße 8 from outside and met the lady who lives upstairs. 22. The Prince told Herrmann that I must have the apartment and that the price should be considerate. When Herrmann begins to hint that, thanks to the services I still render by accompanying the Prince here and there, I should interrupt him: “No, I do not want a preferential price. I want to pay what is due.” Then Frau Lauterbach tells me: 85 marks a month. Lunch at Schauroth’s, where Gödela Keyserling suddenly announces herself. A while at Wauer’s. Letter to Margrit for her birthday on the 24th. 23. Lunch at Schauroth’s. With Frau Lauterbach at Zimmerstraße 8. The apartment is lovely with Hardenberg’s furniture, but so small and without any extra rooms that I would have to part with much of my furniture. I do not know whether I would regret it. I postpone the move until 1 March. Spoke with Glenz. With Bodelschwingh and Gustav. Scheuerhof. 24. At Klöss’s, filling in lower left wisdom tooth. L. G. [?] Encounter with Walter Bundschuh. I have the idea of sending the surplus furniture to Otto R. if he wants it. 25. The Grand Duke’s seventieth birthday. Lunch at Wolfsgarten with Prinz Ludwig; also Prinzessin Heinrich, Thea Ledebur and her daughter. Prinz Ludwig wants a young successor for Hardenberg, especially considering Herrmann’s age. Byck was suggested to him; he does not want Wilbrand. His idea is Oldershausen, his chief of staff during the mobilization. He will come to Wolfsgarten on Tuesday. Hereditary Prinz Hohenlohe had a son yesterday. Ludwig told me that Herrmann saw Lautenschläger, released from prison, at Frau von Lichtenberg’s. He will settle in Frankfurt. Herrmann explained to him that Prinz Ludwig could do nothing for him. 26. Yesterday the Ludwigs [“Lous”] advised me to take the floor above as well and rent two rooms. Georgina will live on the ground floor! Lunch at Schauroth’s. Lachmann for tea. At 20:00 we gather at Frau Merck’s. Commemoration for our dead. The employees and servants were there too. Westermann recited the Grand Duke’s poems. Inge Selzam sang his songs. The decorations caught fire, and Prinz Lou showed courage putting it out. 27. At 12:52 with Fräulein von Rotsmann to Langen; expecting Betta Bellersheim. At Wolfsgarten with General Müller and his daughter. I stayed for dinner. Talked with Ludwig about the Brabant family and learned that a lady-in-waiting, Forstner, had a child by Landgrave Ernst Ludwig. She is buried in Arheilgen and must have been a daughter of Forstner-Grävenitz. 28. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Tea at the Heidis’ with an actress. 29. Letter to Alice. The Oldershausens have declined. With Prinz Lou at Wolfsgarten. Returned at 16:00. They will see the world from a distance at Wolfsgarten. 30. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Bad news from Caputh, which he learned from Otto Suermondt. Departed at 17:38 and at 18:12 from Frankfurt; with Lachmann in Falkenstein. Frau von Gozani and Herr von Estorff. Returned from Kronberg at 22:25 and Frankfurt at 23:21.
December. 1. December. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Dinner at Wauer’s with Frau Weber. Haircut. 2. Cemetery. Lunch at Schauroth’s. I postpone my departure until Sunday evening, since Prinz Lou writes that I should come to Wolfsgarten with the Oldershausens on Sunday. Long, rather fruitless argument in the street with Gustav. With Prinz Ludwig and Professor Köser, who will teach Prinzessin Peggy German at Wolfsgarten. Returned at 15:00. Letter from Alice. 3. At the Schauroths’. Lunch for Ly’s birthday, which I do not attend, but I send chocolate. Thirtieth anniversary of Mother’s death. 4. Visit from Lachmann, who has become a Rittmeister. Yesterday at the Christmas dinner he was told that Max Willich is in prison. At Wolfsgarten at 12:30. The Oldershausen couple. Prinz Lou stays alone with him and me and asks Oldershausen whether he will take over Hardenberg’s work. Oldershausen will ask his bank to give him time to learn about business in Darmstadt and at the same time interest the bank in it. Oldershausen gives me the impression of great energy and intelligence, and I believe I can congratulate Prinz Lou on his choice if Oldershausen accepts. Returned to Darmstadt at 17:00 and packed. At Scheuerhof with Gustav and Heidi. Heidi takes me to the station. Departed at 23:03; at 0:20 from Frankfurt, rather full compartment. In Potsdam at 8:00. Adolf at the station; taxi. 5. To Dietrich-Eckart-Straße 14. Ly [?]. The house has cost Adolf a great deal, but at least it has turned out very handsome and comfortable. Walk with Adolf. 6. Stever, Else and Magnus in the afternoon. 7. Tea at the Negenborns’. Bridge. 8. 9. The Boyne couple for tea. 10. Tea at the Dietrichs’, where Wichard was too; we had not seen him since his wedding. 11. The young maid makes us laugh when she explains that she has to write in her diary. After a discussion, Adolf says Wichard should bring his wife here only when she comes to Berlin. 12. Lunch at Wühlisch’s with Frau von Schönberg and Irmchen. 13. In Berlin at Suermondt’s at 15:00. At Bendlerstraße 31 at 19:00. Saxons’ dinner. I sit between Adolf and Etztorf. Also Falkenhausen, Plötz, Oppen, Traugott Jagow, Winterfeld, Foretsch, Gayl, Herzberg, Görtzke, etc. Returned at midnight. 14. Tea at Negenborn’s. Dinner with Adolf. Palast Braustübl. 15. Annemarie and Wichard for dinner. It is alarming how poorly Wichard looks. 16. Dinner at the Negenborns’ with Gräfin Bismarck and Fräulein Dunker. 17. Cold at 10:00. The house is heated very badly. 18. Letter to Alice. Bitter cold. 19. At the station with Adolf. Departed at 13:00. Changed trains at Kreiensen. One-hour delay. From Frankfurt on a slow, unheated train. Arrived around 1:00. The stove had gone out! 20. At the welfare office. Dietz dead. With secretary Fraedmann [?], ground floor, room eleven, about my second-class pass. Lunch at Schauroth’s with Käthe. At the palace with Prinz Ludwig. Dinner at Schauroth’s. Käthe. 21. At Külp’s. A piece of the lower left wisdom tooth broke off. To Wolfsgarten with Prinz Ludwig! Returned at 15:30 with Lou and my presents: Häberlein and Buxhoeveden’s book. The wisdom tooth filling comes out. 22. At Klöss’s. Nerve treatment on the wisdom tooth. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Errands. Haircut. 23. At Klöss’s. Temporary filling. Lunch at Schauroth’s. Taxi to the station at 17:38. Departure. Long stop at Louisa; I expect to miss the train in Frankfurt, but it is delayed. First I wait outside, then in the waiting room, where a figure passes me whom I think I know. It is hard to find a chair. At last, at 22:00, the arrival of the 18:36 train is announced! I find an empty compartment with little light. We set off at 23:00. At Würzburg I get into a sleeper, where I am alone and sleep until 11:00. Arrived at 15:00. Westbahnhof [Vienna]. 24. Difficult to find a carriage. At last I share one with two women and a child. Pension Schneider, Getreidemarkt 7, entrance on Dreihufeisengasse, where Lachmann is waiting for me. He had a very adventurous journey and lost the luggage he had checked. I have a lovely, well-heated room. Dinner at the nearby Pilsner Stube. I spend the rest of the evening listening to Lachmann reading aloud. 25. Lachmann goes to the station and I to St Stephen’s Cathedral. Walk together around the Hofburg. Lunch at Opern-Schwemme. Walk to Fleischmarkt. Dinner at Lindenrestaurant. Coffee. 26. Alone to the Augustinerkirche, Michaelerkirche, Schottenkirche and via Renngasse to the Burgtheater, where Lachmann joined me. His suitcase arrived. Back to the Augustinerkirche, where I nearly fell because I did not see the steps. Dinner at Meissl und Schadn Schlemme. At the Belvedere and Südbahnhof, then Café Bristol. At 19:20 Lachmann left for Rax. Dinner at Meissl und Schadn Schlemme. 27. National Museum; saw the beautiful paintings. Speisehaus on Mariahilferstraße. Coffee at O K. Waited for Lachmann at the Schlemme, where he arrived at 21:00. 28. Museum with Lachmann. Guided tour of goldsmith’s work and paintings. Lunch at Meissl und Schadn. Café Josefstadt. Theater in Josefstadt, “My Friend Jack” by Somerset Maugham with Diehl. Café on the corner. 29. Czernin Gallery, closed. National Museum, Egyptian and Greek departments. Lunch at Café Lehar. Lachmann at the Burgtheater. I go to the post office and Griechenbeisl. Herr Salkammer. 30. Took the luggage to the station. Lunch at Griechenbeisl. Errands. Café Favoritengasse. Skala cinema, “Napoleon Is to Blame for Everything” by Götz. Very funny. Dinner at OK. Heavy snowfall. By tram to the station. Departed in the sleeper at 21:35. 31. Arrived two hours late, at 9:00, in Innsbruck. Taxi to Pension Hindenburgplatz. Lunch at Grauer Bär. Café Bozener Platz. Dinner mediocre. Ottohof.
